books.section: The New Left, Feminism, and the Counterculture

source: original; stimulus is an original account drawn from the grounding books

stimulus.source_note: Original account drawn from the grounding books: Barron’s Ch. 10, ‘New Left Versus Old Left’; 5 Steps Ch. 27. March details verified against Smithsonian Magazine and the Bill of Rights Institute.
stimulus.text:
Account of the Yippies and the 1967 March on the Pentagon, drawn from the grounding books and verified against Smithsonian Magazine accounts.

On October 21, 1967, more than 100,000 protesters gathered near the Lincoln Memorial in Washington to oppose the Vietnam War, and about 50,000 marched to the Pentagon. Abbie Hoffman, a founder of the Youth International Party — the Yippies — vowed to levitate the Pentagon by psychic energy until it turned orange and the war ended. The Yippies used street theater: they nominated a pig for president and threw money from the gallery of the New York Stock Exchange.

The New Left defined itself against the Old Left’s disciplined, labor-centered organizing. The Old Left had focused on workplace issues and union halls; the New Left focused on participatory democracy and on cultural and social issues, and it organized on college campuses rather than in factories.

stem: The Yippies’ theatrical protests reflected the New Left’s break with

options.text: the civil rights movement of the early 1960s
options.misconception: Background: The New Left learned from the civil rights movement; it did not break with it.

options.text: the Old Left’s disciplined, labor-centered organizing

options.misconception: The Pentagon march was an antiwar protest. The Yippies were part of that movement.
Background: The women’s movement grew from the same circles as the New Left.

rationales.A: The passage says the New Left defined itself against the Old Left, not against civil rights. Background: The civil rights movement was its ally and model.
rationales.B: The passage says the New Left defined itself against the Old Left’s disciplined, labor-centered organizing, choosing theater and participatory democracy instead.
rationales.C: The Yippies were part of the antiwar movement: the Pentagon march opposed the war. They did not break with it.
rationales.D: Background: The women’s movement grew out of the New Left’s own circles. The Yippies did not break with it.
rationales.general:
1. The Yippies used street theater: levitating the Pentagon, nominating a pig.
2. Theater is not union-hall discipline: it is spectacle meant to be seen.
3. The passage says the New Left defined itself against the Old Left’s labor-centered organizing.
4. The break was about style and setting: campuses and streets instead of factories.
Remember: A movement’s style is a clue to its roots: theater points to the campus, not the union hall.
